name: richmond-flood-demo
label: SIMULATION: seeded scenario, not live data
gauge_label: scenario value, not a live USGS reading

events.label: 911 call from a bus in Shockoe Bottom
events.explain: A 911 call from a bus in Shockoe Bottom. The Listener shows the transcript (left), Muse Spark reads it into a new incident, the three agents vote and it becomes #1 in the queue. The recommendation now sends a swift water team and an ambulance there. Press ▶ for the next step.

events.label: Citizen photo of Dock St
events.explain: A citizen photo of Dock St. SAM 3.1 outlines the flooded street and counts the vehicles in the water (boxes on the photo, blue area on the map); Muse Wonder judges the depth and that cars cannot get through, so Dock St closes (black). The swarm re-votes and the route changes to cross the 14th St (Mayo) Bridge instead. Press ▶ for the next step.
events.footprint_note: Assumed area the photo covers (around Dock St); the test image is not georeferenced.

events.label: River gauge update
events.explain: The river gauge rises to 11.8 ft, near the 12 ft sample trigger. The access check re-scores the low-lying incidents and the plan is recomputed. Press ▶ for the next step.

events.label: 911 call: man trapped in his car at Hull St
events.explain: A new 911 call: a man trapped in his car in the Hull St underpass. The agents score it critical. Every team is already out, so the solver reroutes: Swift Water Team 2 and Ambulance 1 go to Hull St, Swift Water Team 3 takes over the bus, and the lower-priority Manchester dialysis transfer waits, with the reason shown. Press Approve & Dispatch, then ▶.

events.label: Swift Water Team 1: Riverside residents safe
events.text: All five residents at Riverside Apartments are out and safe.
events.explain: Swift Water Team 1 reports the Riverside residents are safe. The incident leaves the queue, every agent drops it, and its boat and ambulance stand down, back in service. The solver re-plans: Ambulance 2 goes to Hull St so Ambulance 1 can return to the Manchester dialysis patient.

intro: Five incidents are already open. Each card shows three votes (Intake, Vision, Access check) and their consensus; the queue is ranked by it. The right panel is the swarm's current recommendation. Watch the next event arrive. Press ▶ (or the → key) to bring in the first report.
outro: Your turn. Read the recommendation on the right (what, why, confidence, tradeoff) and press Approve & Dispatch. The English and Spanish public alert appears below it. Then press ▶ for the next report.
approved: Approved: units are dispatched (they move on the map) and the alert is out. Press ▶ for the next report.
outro_2: Your turn again. The freed units cover the waiting call. Review the new recommendation and press Approve & Dispatch.
final: That is the full loop: detect, prioritize, decide, dispatch, communicate, and again when new information arrives. Press Restart to run it again.
gauge_time_note: Each gauge reading carries the scenario hour it represents; the 50-second demo compresses about an hour of river rise.
